This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json adbbc5d01e76ac7ed561dec1c95592320acb8565` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ca1594ded0855f91029cc0b91b02fdee5ede841f` — the merge of head `46e1c81727aee80f722f4b4554b01250211bbbfb` into base `adbbc5d01e76ac7ed561dec1c95592320acb8565`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ca1594ded0855f91029cc0b91b02fdee5ede841f && git checkout ca1594ded0855f91029cc0b91b02fdee5ede841f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin adbbc5d01e76ac7ed561dec1c95592320acb8565 46e1c81727aee80f722f4b4554b01250211bbbfb && git checkout -B drift-repro adbbc5d01e76ac7ed561dec1c95592320acb8565 && git merge --no-ff 46e1c81727aee80f722f4b4554b01250211bbbfb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json adbbc5d01e76ac7ed561dec1c95592320acb8565
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs adbbc5d01e76ac7ed561dec1c95592320acb8565` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: 164/164 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `46e1c81727aee80f722f4b4554b01250211bbbfb`

Isolated at-tier reviewer subagent, run by the `domain:spec` seat-4 session; every one of its 164 transcript turns served at the tier the constant names. First review of this head. The seat's provisional reading of ruling item 4 (the same sentence, with the location carried by the issue path) is judged under (b). For the two DELIBERATE CORRECTIONS (`.changeset/19757-equality-slot-array-refused.md`, `.changeset/19888-analytics-implicit-array.md`) this is the same-head at-tier PASS that names each note and judges each changed sentence; the maintainer's standing words in this seat's chat, 「changeset 你看着更新就行」, cover the correction of pending notes. Adopted by the seat 2026-09-24T23:34Z. The record below is the reviewer's, unedited except the two header lines.


### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #19889 body and all 5 comments (ruling `5805248669`, services note `5819407923`, claim `5820755955`, os-dev-report `5823840715`); ruling 乙 `5793368540`; PR #20047 body, 12 files, diff, 1 bot comment, 0 review comments; PR #20008 (merged 2026-09-24T18:24:47Z, `14add487b4f72f48a6ec772e1779f3ad33934eba`) and PR #19882 (merged 14:44:23Z, `753672152851f4da52d85b543f72514467b548ee`), both ancestors of the PR base `a0920b42dc33efadc483f5112da36cfa53124cbb` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` yes/yes); report.json is byte-equivalent to comment `5823840715`. No worktree or probe was run; every reading is `git show`/`git grep`/`git diff` on `refs/review/pr-20047` (= head) and `origin/main` (`5581d3000f27daa19991cf9d13d5ad1ed8cf8913`).

(a) Accept set, ruling A items 1–3. `FilterConditionSchema` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).and(z.object({$and,$or,$not})).superRefine(checkFilterConditionComparands)` (filter.zod.ts:1850-1869 at head), so field values are judged only by the walk. The walk (filter.zod.ts:1659-1736): a field entry whose value is an array is refused at `depth === 0` with path `[key]` (1675-1684, empty array included since `Array.isArray([])`); an operator spec's `$eq` array is refused at `depth === 0` with path `[key,'$eq']` (1697-1706); `$`-keys are skipped (1669) and `$and`/`$or`/`$not` members re-enter `FilterConditionSchema` (1853-1855), so each member is judged at depth 0 of its own pass with nested issue paths; a no-`$` spec recurses at `depth+1` (1687-1691) and is not judged. The face `assertListComparandShapes` (filter-comparand-shape.ts:717-775 at head) walks `$and`/`$or`/`$not` and top-level fields, refuses an array spec (757-759) and `$eq` array (770-773), and returns on a no-`$` spec (764). Reach is identical. Nothing else moves: the `$eq` arm's `continue` skips only the `$icontains` (`FILTER_TEXT_COMPARAND_OPERATOR`, :1574) and preset checks (`PRESET_JUDGED_ORDERING_OPS = $gt,$gte,$lt,$lte`, :1564; `$between`, :1724), none of which ever judged `$eq`. Scalars, `null`, `Date`, `{ $field }` (an operator map whose only op is `$field`, not `$eq`), `$in`/`$nin`/`$between` lists, `$ne` lists and nested-relation specs still pass, and the record-of-unknown returns the document unchanged (pinned §4, `expect(result.data).toEqual(where)`, test:202). `FieldOperatorsSchema.$eq` and `EqualityOperatorSchema.$eq` share `equalityComparandSchema()` (filter.zod.ts:285-289, 297, 1453), `z.any().superRefine` refusing only `Array.isArray(value)`. The pairing rule exists on `origin/main`: `orderingComparandSchema` is used by both copies (filter.zod.ts:411, 423-432 and 1427-1432 at main). `EqualityOperatorSchema` is composed into no carrier (`git grep EqualityOperatorSchema` at head: only docblocks and the entry), so its narrowing is beyond the ruling's letter but on the file's declared pairing rule, and it is named in the entry surface and changeset. `NormalizedFilterSchema` narrows as a consequence: `normalizedFieldConditionSchema = z.record(z.string(), FieldOperatorsSchema)` (filter.zod.ts:2067-2070). Census: my spot-check `git grep -E "(filter|where|runtimeFilter|having|relatedListFilter)\s*:\s*\{\s*\w+\s*:\s*\["` over `examples/**`, `apps/**`, `packages/**/src/**`, `skills/**` excluding tests at head hits only two comment lines (metadata-core engine-delete-dispatch.ts:295, engine-update-dispatch.ts:661); `$eq: [` hits are prose and MongoDB `$cond` aggregation expressions. Consistent with the report's 0 shipped instances; deployed metadata NOT MEASURED (disclosed). "Refused loudly, never dropped" holds: a `custom` issue fails the parse, nothing strips a key (no `.strip`/`.catch`/`.transform` on the record side), and no non-test consumer parses `FilterConditionSchema` directly with a fallback (`git grep -E "FilterConditionSchema\.(safeParse|catch|parse)\("` over `packages/**/src` at main, excluding tests: 0 hits); carriers reach it through their type schemas: metadata-protocol 422 `INVALID_METADATA` from zod issues (protocol.ts:707, 973), REST selection door 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` with `selection.FIELD: message` (rest/analytics-selection-door.ts:133-171), runtime analytics body `AnalyticsQueryRequestSchema.safeParse` to 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` (runtime/domains/analytics.ts:63-76).

(b) Item 4, message equality. The face's text is byte-identical to `origin/main`: old inline assembly (`${position} requires a single comparable value, but received an array (${shapePreview(value)}) at ${path}. For "one of these values" use {"$in": […]} (authoring: ${inSpellings.join(', ')}); ...UNFILTERED result set.`) versus `arrayEqualityComparandMessage(value, {op, field, path})` (filter-comparand-refusal-text.ts:133-145) with `IN_OPERATOR_SPELLINGS = ['in']` (:38) equal to the old `LIST_COMPARAND_OPERATORS.get('$in')`; the face always passes `field` and `path` (filter-comparand-shape.ts:682), so its `position` and ` at path` clauses render exactly as before. The schema door passes no `path`, so the message is the face's minus the ` at where.FIELD` clause; on the `$eq` slot no `field`, so minus ` on field "X"` too. Truth at every depth: the implicit arm names the local key (`{ field: key }`, :1680) and the `$eq` arm the local key (:1702), which is the correct field for a `$and`/`$or`/`$not` member; the issue path (`$and.0.tags`, `$not.tags.$eq`, `measures.0.filter.stage.$eq`) carries the location. Pin §3 (test:128-157) asserts the face clause is present exactly once and the schema string equals `face.message.replace(location, '.')` over 8 shapes, and the slot row equals the face minus both clauses. Recommendation A keeps one constant and the same words, and a fixed `where.` prefix would be false for a saved document and for combinator members; I concur with the seat's provisional reading. One non-blocking observation under ③ on the closing sentence.

(c) Carriers. `Engine{Query,Update,Delete,Aggregate,Count}OptionsSchema.where` and `DataEngineVectorFindRequestSchema.where` are `z.union([z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()), FilterConditionSchema])` (data-engine.zod.ts:100, 234, 329, 354, 414, 1314 at main), so the open first arm parses the shape. These are runtime call options and a wire request, not stored metadata; item 3 names stored filters and their next save; the face refuses at the engine lowering seam. Correctly outside item 3, and disclosed as position (2) in the entry, the changeset (:25) and the PR body. `EngineAggregateOptionsSchema.having` is `FilterConditionSchema` directly (:376) and refuses. The entry's surface list matches the carrier grep at head exactly: dataset.zod.ts:191/343, dashboard.zod.ts:872/1285 (`GlobalFilterOptionsFromSchema`), report.zod.ts:239 (`JoinedReportBlockSchema`)/347 (`ReportSchema`), field.zod.ts:1529/1634 (`summaryOperations`), solution-blueprint.zod.ts:71, data/analytics.zod.ts:685, api/analytics.zod.ts:549, query.zod.ts:295/522/571, data-engine.zod.ts:376, filter.zod.ts:1911 (`QueryFilterSchema.where`).

(d) ADR-0087. New entry `18.filter-equality-array-comparand-refused-at-save.ts` (id, surface, replacement, reason, acceptanceCriteria all present); marker `adr-0087: registered filter-equality-array-comparand-refused-at-save` (changeset:46); the gate's `breakingDeclaration` reads BREAKING + bang + `clause-②-narrowing` (check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:626-634) and requires exactly one marker, which is present. Every checked sentence is true at head: the reach paragraph (verified above), position (1) (analytics `forEachWhereFieldEntry` recurses a no-`$` spec, service-analytics/src/strategies/filter-normalizer.ts:1588-1591 at main, and the normalizer flattens nested relations to dotted members, :1125, :1425), position (2) (the union above), the two request doors (verified above), 422 `INVALID_METADATA`. Corrected entry: the "four ways" sentence matches the pre-#20008 behaviour the pending `.changeset/19888-analytics-implicit-array.md` records at :23-26; "hands each equality-slot list to the shared face" is `assertNoListInEqualitySlot` calling `assertListComparandShapes` (filter-normalizer.ts:1655-1663 at main); "that door alone also refuses a list inside a nested-relation condition" is the recursion at :1588. `registry.ts`: I re-derived the whole `semantic:18` region (166 entries) from the entry files at head using the generator's own rules (build-migration-registry.ts:179-183 leading `//` run, :185-191 literal, :253 sort by id, :258-266 four-space indent plus trailing comma) and it is byte-identical to the region between the markers at head (8663 lines each, `REGISTRY semantic:18 REGION == DERIVED`). `refused` sorts before `refused-at-save`, as emitted.

(e) Changesets. New note: `"@objectstack/spec": minor`, `fix(spec)!:` summary, `**BREAKING**` banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, marker; every sentence checked is true at head (reach, carriers, both request doors, "strips nothing", `$ne` unjudged, the three dropped-refinement sites). Correction 1, `.changeset/19757-equality-slot-array-refused.md:35`: the old sentence ("`FilterConditionSchema` still parses `{ field: [...] }`... still publishes") is false at head; the new one is true (same words minus the path-borne location; the sibling entry exists). The rest of the note stays true: the table row and :48 describe the before-state, :25 "the drivers themselves are untouched" and :34 "no `$` key... not descended into" hold. Correction 2, `.changeset/19888-analytics-implicit-array.md:30`: the old "The authoring schema still admits the shape, so such a document still publishes" is false at head; the new sentence is true, including "One position is judged only here: a list inside a nested relation... still publishes" (schema door depth greater than 0 is unjudged; analytics recurses). No other pending note at head or at main states the schema door admits this shape: `.changeset/20010-analytics-where-face-arms.md:26` ("The authoring schema still admits the shapes") concerns null list members, null ordering comparands, blank/null `$between` endpoints and a scalar `$in`, none of which this PR refuses; `18232`'s "schema door" lines concern date ranges. `check-empty-changeset` refuses both edits by name as the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class (script:121-133; CI annotations on `Check Changeset` name both files with that remedy). Clause-② consistency: `readClause2Line` treats the arm as optional (clause2-line.mjs:80-101); `check-changeset-no-major` reads the PR body's value (`no`, level axis not engaged) and `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the changeset's arm (`narrowing`, breaking, marker required and present). Same value, consistent for both readers.

(f) `packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-refusal-text.ts` is imported only by `filter-comparand-shape.ts:311` and `filter.zod.ts:9`; absent from `data/index.ts` (grep: 0), from `package.json` `exports`, and from every `api-surface/*.json` (data.json records names only, `EqualityOperatorSchema (const)` unchanged; `api-surface-signatures.json` records `define*` signatures only). No api-surface file is in the diff. Baseline: the ledger's own description says it is hand-edited with no `gen:` script and `build-schemas.ts` fails until the line moves; at head the map holds 207 entries and 574 sites (computed), equal to `measured` (207/574), which is exactly what `scripts/dropped-refinements.test.ts:369-371` pins; the three added sites are the three narrowed `$eq` slots, on the same site pattern as the existing `$in`/`$nin` rows.

(g) Pins. 46 tests (9+3+11+19+4) matches 46/46. Leg arithmetic against the file: A (implicit arm off) = §1 5 implicit rows + the two-slot test + §3 5 implicit rows + the remedy test + §5 `filter.stage` + widget/report = 14; B ($eq off) = 3+1+3+2 = 9; C (slot off) = §2 3 + §3 slot row = 4; D (location printed on the implicit arm) = the 5 implicit §3 rows = 5; E = the one implicit nested-relation control; F = only `the operator slot accepts every scalar and null` parses `$eq: null` through `FieldOperatorsSchema` = 1. Each leg's count is what the file's structure produces, so the pins guard the arms and the reach.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: minor` with `**BREAKING**`, `fix(spec)!:` and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is what AGENTS.md:1072-1084 at main prescribes (a `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; `check-changeset-no-major` forbids `major` in the launch window; a breaking changeset must carry FROM-TO and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, both present). No public export added or moved. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- non-blocking: the closing sentence of the shared remedy ("The filter was NOT applied, and an unapplied filter would have returned the UNFILTERED result set") is a query-time statement now printed at save time; it is not false (a refused filter is unapplied), it is what item 1's "SAME remedy text" orders, and the module docblock (:90-93) states the reason. Recorded, not a defect.
- non-blocking: the `FieldOperatorsSchema.$eq` slot drops ` on field "X"` as well as the location clause (disclosed in deviation 1); every stored carrier goes through the `FilterConditionSchema` arm, which names the field, so only a direct operator-map parse (and `NormalizedFilterSchema`, whose issue path carries the field) sees the shorter sentence.
- non-blocking: PR body carries `Clause-②: no` (the claim's line) while the changeset carries `no (narrowing)`; AGENTS.md:1084 says the changeset "also carries the PR's Clause-② line". Same value, arm optional, gates consistent.
- non-blocking: files outside the claim's named surface are `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json` (gate-prescribed hand-edit) and `.changeset/19888-analytics-implicit-array.md` (services lane's note, DELIBERATE CORRECTION); both disclosed and the second awaits a person's confirmation on the PR, per the gate's own remedy.
- non-blocking, out-of-scope finding confirmed real: `{ account: { region: ['a'] } }` in a dataset or measure filter passes the schema door (depth greater than 0 unjudged, mirroring the face) and is refused at chart time by the analytics door (recursion at filter-normalizer.ts:1588). It is the same publish-clean-fail-later class on the analytics-only carriers; refusing it at the shared door would refuse a deep-equality comparand the face and engine accept, so it needs its own decision (carrier-specific refinement or the analytics door stopping its descent). Disclosed in the entry (position 1), the new changeset (:24) and the 19888 correction.
- non-blocking: `main` has moved 10 commits past base `a0920b42dc` (report said 8), none touching any file in this diff (`git log a0920b42dc..origin/main -- diff files`: empty); `registry.ts` untouched on main since base. #20010 landed in that window and does not change any sentence here.
- CI at head, read twice: first fetch 32 runs, 12 success / 16 in progress / 3 skipped / 1 failure; re-fetch 16 success / 12 in progress / 3 skipped / 1 failure. The failure is `Check Changeset` (run 36071687724), whose annotations name exactly the two corrected notes with the COLLISION-vs-DELIBERATE-CORRECTION remedy; red by design until confirmed. Successes include `Type Check · source gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check PR Size`, the claim/branch guards. Test Core 1-6, Lint and Repo Gates, Type Check workspace/consumer/debt, Dogfood 1-3, Temporal Conformance were still in progress; not awaited, no gate family re-run. PR is a draft, `mergeable_state: blocked`.
- The report's suites, gates and ablation logs are claims; the ablation counts and the registry are the two I could re-derive, and both hold.
